executive_assessment.text: The CCDR projects that by 2070, 98% of Benin’s territory could face extreme temperatures under a 2.7°C global-warming pathway associated with current policies.
In EHCVM 2018/19, 21.4% of households reported a climate-induced shock during the previous three years; 10.5% reported flood impacts and 12% drought impacts.

geographic_notes.text: Northern Benin; Southern Benin; Rural and urban areas; Sahelian countries (source-mentioned origin of in-migration): The CCDR says climatic pressures could widen rural-urban and north-south gaps, compounding northern insecurity and displacement, including Sahelian in-migration.

Coastal Benin; Sèmè-Kpodji; Cotonou; Abomey-Calavi; Ouidah; Grand-Popo: The NDC identifies 30 communes in the coastal zone, five on the seafront, and reports shoreline retreat of 12–30 metres per year at critical points alongside flood, drought, wind and sea-level risks.

known_gaps.text: No independently inspected subnational dataset was used to quantify current displacement or insecurity exposure.
